title: How many bands worked the District
summary: Barnes says about two dozen bands played in the Red District, in houses and honky-tonks.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: Well, let's go back to the district. Wow. How much of the work was in the district? Would you say many musicians were there? Not too many?
Yeah, good many musicians. Most every house had it. Had music up there. Every house, you know every place. Gammon houses.
You said there were about a dozen bands there, or two dozen?

Around the neighborhood. All through where Crosswood, where the Thomas Station is now. Over on Ramport Street. Go down to what you call St. Claude Street there. Basin Street there. What the name you call it. Way back to Robson Street. Come back to Corney, St. Louis. And you go all the way back and you hit on the other side there. You had the Red District. I played all through there. I played all through there. All in the tunks. The cabras in the tunks too, in the barms.
